articleTitle: The Canadian Calibration Network
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings. The National Research Council (NRC) and the Standards Council of Canada (SCC) are planning to set up a system for accrediting secondary calibration laboratories. To join the system, laboratories will have to demonstrate the ability to make accurate calibrations traceable to national measurement standards. The aim is to serve industry, commerce and trade by providing a national system of measurement standards compatible with those of Canada's international trading partners. The system, to be known as the Canadian Calibration Network, will be coordinated closely with the SCC National Accreditation Program for Testing Organizations (NAPTO) and the Facility Recognition Program of the Department of National Defence. The presentation will give details on the progress made on the implementation of the network.

articleTitle: Precise Measurement Method for Complex Permittivity of Microwave Dielectric Substrate
abstract: A new technique for the measurement of the complex permittivity of dielectrie substrates using a dielectric resonator is reported. This method is a non-contact measurement using two dielectric resonators which support TE mode. This paper describes some examples of measurements.

articleTitle: Improved Cavity Resonance Method For Nondestructive Measurement Of Complex Permittivity Of Dielectric Plate
abstract: An improved cavity resonance method is proposed to measure the complex permittivity of dielectric plate sample nondestructively. A plate sample is clamped by two halves, into which a cavity is cut at the center. The effect of the fringing field is accurately calculated by the Ritz-Galerkin method.

articleTitle: Reducing the Uncertainty in Absolute Volt Determination at ETF in Zagreb
abstract: In up-to-date measurement results, obtained by the ETF Voltage balances, a contribution of uncertainties of the used mass, capacity and voltage standards prevails. Their better calibration, together with a better determination of local gravity acceleration, better measurement of the displacement and with better performances of the balance, promises the total uncertainty of 0.3 ppm to be achieved.

articleTitle: Optical FM Heterodyne Interferometry For Range And Displacement Measurements
abstract: A novel technique of frequency modulated ( FM ) heterodyne interferometer has been realized for measuring remotely the range and the displacement of both specular reflectors and diffuse surface objects using a FM semiconductor laser. The resolution better than 7 um was realized for the range measurement and about 1 nm for the displacement measurement with specular targets for ranges to about 2 m.

articleTitle: A calculable, transportable audio-frequency AC reference standard
abstract: A transportable ac voltage source is described, in which sinusoidal signals are digitally-synthesized in the audio-frequency range. The rms value of the output waveform may be calculated by measuring the dc level of the individual steps used to generate the waveform. The uncertainty of this calculation is typically 10 ppm from 20 Hz - 10 kHz at the 7 V level.

articleTitle: Performance And Its Evaluation Of Optical Tracking Generator/ Optical Frequengy Synthesizer By Semiconductor Lasers
A VHF-UHF wide band field strength standard using a small dipole antenna
abstract: A VHF-UHF range wide band field standard system consistence of a small dipole antenna with a low Q compensation circuit, and antenna factor measurement system using standard coaxial line system has been developed. Its antenna factor is measured by the three antennas method, being within 2dB over 100-500 MHz frequency range, and measurement accuracy better than D.5 dB are obtained.

articleTitle: Improved Cryo-Resistors with Low Temperature Coefficients
Josephon Array Voltage Calibration System: Operational Use and Verification
abstract: A New Josephson Array System Now Maintains The U. S. Legal Volt On A Weekly Basis. The Accuracy Of The I-volt Level Of This System Was Verified To Within 0.03 Ppm In Multiple Tests Against Two Independent Resistive Dividers. The Precision In The Verification Was -limited By Uncertainties In The Divider Instruments.

articleTitle: In search of the best clock
abstract: Because of the increased need for better clock performance than is currently available, this paper addresses some fundamental questions regarding clock metrology. Heretofore, most work has focussed on improving the clocks to meet the increased need. Though this is fundamental and will be addressed in the paper, we will also show that significant gains are available through the algoritbms which process the clock readings and through international comparisons now available via satellite. Proper algorithms for processing seem to be more important than the proportionate attention generally given them. In fact, to date, the only way we have been able to investigate some of the long-term performance aspects of the millisecond pulsar, ESR 1937+21, is by using such optimization algorithms. Since there are indications in the pulsar data of variations which could be explained as arising from the influence of gravity waves, these long-term stability studies take on a new importance. Years of study will probably be necessary to confirm these initial indications, but clearly improved long-term stability of earth-bound clock systems would significantly assist this study.

articleTitle: Determination of the Dissipative Loss in Low-Loss Two-Ports
abstract: The dissipative loss of a reciprocal two-port can be determined from its input reflection coefficients measured while terminating the output with load, short and open circuits, and sliding short. The paper presents a statistical approach applied to minimize random errors of the loss determination.

articleTitle: The Six-Port Four Standards Linear Least Square Calibration Method
abstract: A calibration method using four short air tines with different length is introduced in this paper. It is more precise than Li's method because tesst square principle is used to resolve contradictory equation in the presence of noise [1], and more simple than Hoer's method because only linear equation and formula resolution are used in calculation [2].

articleTitle: New Type LVDT Position Detector
abstract: We describe in this paper two kinds of new type position detector which can be attached to the linear motor for one or two dimensional precise positioning. These detectors give the position signal by the principle of linear variable differential transformer (LVDT), but have quite different structure from the usual type .

articleTitle: Design of High Performance Portable Optically Pumped Cesium Beam Standards
Equivalent Circuit for Imperfect Transmission Line Connectors
abstract: An exact equivalent circuit for a pair of imperfect transmission line connectors is developed. New reference planes are chosen in such a way that all imperfections in the connector pair can be lumped into one connector or the other. This makes it possible to calibrate out imperfections in test port connectors when calibrating network analyzers.

articleTitle: A Measurement of the NBS Electrical Watt in SI Units
abstract: We have measured the NBS electrical watt in SI units by comparing mechanical and electrical power. This measurement of the NBS watt, combined with a measurement of the NBS ohm, gives the NBS volt and ampere, as well as 2e/h, in SI units.

articleTitle: Ultrawide Frequency Response Measurement System Using Optical Heterodyne Detection Method
abstract: An effective system for measuring optical detector bandwidth has been established using the heterodyne detection method utilizing tow DFB-LDs. By controlling the LD temperature, the measurable bandwidth can be extended to beyond several tens GHz without any additional calibration. Included are a comparison of bandwidth measurement methods, features of the developed measurement system, and the measurement results.

articleTitle: Development of the New PTB Highly Accurate AC Power Source
abstract: A highly accurate ac power source for unity power factor with an expected total uncertainty of a few parts in 10/sup 6/ to be used in the power frequency range is described. The rms value of the output voltage is continuously readjusted to a precisely known dc reference voltage using a multijunction thermal converter. A reference current is derived from the output voltage using an accurately known reiistor. The output current of a transconductance amplifier is compared to this reference current by means of a current comparator and continuously readjusted.

articleTitle: A Spatial Encoding Method for Improving the Resolution and Reliability of Laser Interferometers
abstract: A method of improving the resolution and reliability of a laser interferometer which is used for measuring displacement is proposed. By giving code numbers to the divided segments of the interference fringe interval, the theoretical resolution is improved up to 1/170 of the light wave length. As the error caused by environmental noise is not integrated, the reliability is improved.

articleTitle: A Holographic Pattern Measuring System (HPMS) and Its Application to the Thermal Deformation of an Electrical Contact Spring
abstract: The HPMS is a technique developed by the authors which can measure the vibration or deformation of any object by means of the holographic interferogram analysis. This technique was applied to the microscopic displacement of an electric contact spring which was thermally deformed due to contact current. A deformed contact spring shape was obtained with an accuracy of 0.16/spl mu/m, and it was proved that the HPMS was a very good technique for measuring a microscopic movement of the object such as a fretting phenomenon in electric contacts.

articleTitle: Theory and Design of a New Series of Decade Resistors
abstract: Theory and design of a new series of decade resistors are devised. They are based on a minimum number of resistance elements connected in series and having nominal values R, 2R and 3R, where R is the nominal value of resistance per step. The series of decades is derived in a table which starts with a 4-step decade resistor and ends with a 21-step decade.

articleTitle: New Realization of the OHM and FARAD Using the NBS Calculable Capacitor
abstract: The latest results of a new realization of the ohm and farad using the NBS calculable capacitor and associated apparatus will be reported.

articleTitle: Measurement and Sensitivity of a Single-Chip Squid Magnetometer
abstract: We operated a single-chip SQUID magnetometer where all components such as a pickup coil, SQUID sensor, and feedback circuit are integrated in a chip. A CAMAC system was used for displaying the waveform. We also calculated the theoretical sensitivity and compared it with the measured data.

articleTitle: Micro-Computer Controlled Moisture/Permittivity Measurements in Microwave Frequencies
abstract: A microwave system using close-loop technics measures simultaneously the weight and the complex dielectric constant of sample materials heated by strong electric RF fields inside a resonant cavity. The uses of a micro-computer permits to relate, in real time, the moisture content of sample materials exposed to RF fields to the dynamic changes observed in the complex dielectric constant at the test frequency [1].

articleTitle: A Realization Of Fail-Safe Sensor Using Electromagnetic Induction
abstract: This paper describes a realization of fail-safe sensor by using electromagnetic induction. The transducer coils are stationed on a plate for magnifying the sensitivity. The optimum construction for train detection is determined based on measurement patterns. This sensor has two complimentary outputs for the fail-safe processing.

articleTitle: Operational Aspects Of Casa Uno - The Fast Large Scale International GPS Geodetic Network
abstract: For three weeks from January 18 to February 5 of 1988, the most extensive international GPS experiment to date was successfully conducted involving 15 countries, over 30 international institutions and universities, and 43 GPS reoeivers. Global coverage of GPS observations spanned 220/spl deg/ of longitude and 125/spl deg/ in latitude. The experiment was the first civilian effort at implementing an extended international GPS satellite tracking network. The predicted improvement in precise orbit determination is crucial for accurate long baseline geodesy. The collaborative experiment called "CASA UNO" (an acronym for Central and South America, the first experiment), was coordinated and managed by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, under the Geodynamics Program.

articleTitle: Determination of AC-DC Difference in the 0.1 - 100 MHZ Frequency Range
abstract: Thermal voltage converter structures have been modeled theoretically and studied experimentally to determine their ac-dc differences in the 0.1-100 megahertz frequency range.

articleTitle: Industrial experience with an array Josephson junction
abstract: An Array Josephson Junctin (AJJ) has been in operation at Lockheed Missiles & Space Co. (LMSC) since September 1986. The AJJ was fabricated at the U.S. National Bureau of Standards (NBS) in Boulder, Co. It has been used on a routine basis for calibration of primary solid state reference standards near 1.0 volts since January 1987. Uncertainties at this voltage level are presently estimated at less than 0.3 ppm.

articleTitle: An international comparison of dc voltage at 1 V and 10 V using solid-state reference standards
abstract: An intercomparison of dc voltage at 1 V and 10 V using solid-state reference standards has been carried out. This intercomparison was thought to test the suitability of these standards as transfer standards and to compare the as-maintained units of different laboratories especially at the 10 V level. First results are presented.

articleTitle: The Next Tenfold Increase in Accuracy of the Electrical Base Units
abstract: This decade has seen more than a tenfold improvement towards uncertainties of 0.1 ppm in the realisation, maintenance and dissemination of the ohm, volt and watt. Prospects for a further improvement to 0.01 ppm seem bright if the present level of effort is sustained. This paper is aimed at promoting discussion on the best routes to follow.

articleTitle: Laser Diode Interferometer For Small Displacement and Sound Pressure Measurements
abstract: A laser diode interferometer for small displacement measurement in a low frequency range was constructed using two Acoustooptic Tunable Filters with slightly different frequencies of the diffracted light. A sound pressure measurement of the condenser microphone using a combination of a polarization maintaining fiber and this laser diode interferometer are proposed for application.

articleTitle: Accurate Thin Film Multijunction Thermal Converter on a Silicon Chip
An optically linked electric and magnetic field sensor for poynting vector measurements in the near field of radiating sources
abstract: An improved, single-element antenna sensing technique is described which can simultaneously measure the electric (E) field, magnetic (H) field, and time-dependent Poynting vector of electromagnetic (EM) fields. Two rf voltages are produced which, along with relative phase and frequency informaiton, are transmitted to a remotely located analyzer by a pair of matched fiber optic downlinks.

articleTitle: The Determination of Yp' (low) at the ETL
Precision 1MHz capacitance standards using loss-free-type three-terminal capacitors
abstract: A methods for precise extrapolation of low frequency values of standard capacitors to higher frequencies has been developed. Theory, procedure and some experimental results, including both unshielded loss-free-type three-terminal capacitors constructed for this purpose and very small sized ceramic capacitors used as a reference standard for the measurement, are described.

articleTitle: Development of a Spectroscopic Measuring System for Time-Varying Optical Spectra Using a CCD Image Sensor
A New EM Fundamental Constant: The Electric Conductivity of Background Space
The Design Of Kalman Smoothers For Global Positioning Data
abstract: Measurements of clocks aboard Global Positioning System (GPS) satellites as well as GPS system time are made many times per day at time standards laboratories around the world according to a tracking schedule issued by the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (International Bureau of Weights and Measures). We compute Kalman smoothed estimates of clocks in the standards labs to define a global time base, then compute Kalman smoothed estimates of GPS clocks against this time base. Biases in measurements repeated once per sidereal day produce apparent diurnal effects in the data. A composite time and frequency Kalman estimator is used here. This allows updates of clocks at time intervals less than one day while aliasing diurnal variations.

articleTitle: A Study Of The NBS Time Scale Algorithm
abstract: Since 1968 the NBS time scale algorithm has been generating a clock which is theoretically better than any of the individual clocks in its ensemble. In the last few years, thanks to the Global Positioning System, we have been able to measure the time difference between the NBS time scale algorithm and the other time standards around the world. We are able to study long term stability of the order of years, and short term stability of the order of days. We now have estimated fractional frequency stabilities for averaging times out to a year of 1*10/sup -14/. This paper studies the behavior of the algorithm from a theoretical point of view, characterizing its performance.

articleTitle: Standard Power Sensor in Millimeter Wave Band
abstract: R.F. power sensors qualified for using as power standards must incorporate refinements not available in commercial devices. The poster describes a waveguide bolometer mount in millimeter band (WR-28), employing metallic thin film, on mica substrate, as sensitive element with high efficiency. Bolometer mount also incorporates a thin film thermopile, type T, and a reference cold thermal load, for effective efficiency measurements in a new microcalorimeter.

articleTitle: Measurement of Electromagnetic Interference from DC - Switching Relays
abstract: By using a spectrum analyzer as a receiver of fixed tuning type, frequency spectra of noise current causing by a relay switching can be separated in opening and in closing. They were reasured and also corpared with frequency spectra of the radiation interference field strength.

articleTitle: Development of injection voltage technique for absolute calibration of inductive voltage divider
abstract: Experimental set-up used for the absolute calibration of inductive voltage divider using injection voltage is described. The total uncertainty obtained in the calibration is of the order of 1x10 -8 at 1kHz.

articleTitle: Angular Navigation on Short Baselines Using Phase Delay Interferometry
abstract: Phase delay interferometry on baselines of tens or hundreds of kilometers can provide angular navigation capabilities competitive with group delay interferometry on intercontinental baselines, due to the mach higher precision of the phase delay datatype. Results are presented for two recent short baseline experiments, with baseline lengths of 6 and 253 km, showing delay residuals of 10 psec or less for angularly close sources.

articleTitle: Accurate RF Voltage Measurements Using a Sampling Voltage Tracker
abstract: The rf voltage measurement capability of an equivalent time sampling system is described. The frequency range investigated is 1 to 100 NHz. Over this range, the measured errors, determined by ac/dc thermal transfer, are within the stated uncertainties presently provided by NBS for thermal converter calibrations. The system offers several advantages over conventional thermal transfer techniques: ac/dc transfers are not required, loading and transmission line problems are reduced, and direct measurement of voltages from 2 V to as low as 10 mV are possible.

articleTitle: Heat Propagation In Differential Thermal Analysis System Using Fiber Optics Teghnology
abstract: This paper reports on the performance of a Michelson interferometer type differential thermal analysis system. In particular, temperature response analysis under heat propagation delay conditions is analyzed. Temperature responses for given continuous and pulsed heat are formulated with high agreement with experimental results, High temperature-measuring sensitivity of the optical fiber thermometer is also experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Six-Port Reflectometer: Influence of Q-Points Position in r-Plane on Sidearm Power Detector Error Propagation
abstract: An attractive feature of the network analyzers based on six-port measurement technique is the high number of equivalent multiport junctions that at least theoretically may be implemented. The paper describes an effort to look for an optimum circuit configuration that minimizes the propagation of the errors due to power detectors.

articleTitle: An Investigation Into The Role Of The Allan Variance In Establishing A Reference Standard Of Voltage
abstract: Allan's ratio test for non-white noise is mathematically equivalent to the F-test for goodness-of-fit. Thus, Allan's test is not strictly a test for non-white noise, but a test for time dependent relationships in the data set. Its usefulness for solid state references is being investigated.

articleTitle: NBS Determination of the Fine-Structure Constant, and of the Quantized Hall Resistance and Josephson Frequency to Voltage Quotient in Si Units
abstract: Results from NBS experiments to realize the ohm and the watt, to determine the proton gyromagnetic ratio and the time dependence of the NBS ohm using the quantum Hall effect, and to maintain the NBS volt using the Josephson effect, are appropriately combined to obtain a highly accurate value of the fine-structure constant and of the quantized Hall resistance in SI units, and accurate values in SI units of the Josephson frequency to voltage quotient, Planck constant, and elementary charge.

articleTitle: New Trench Depth Measurement System with Wavelength-Rapidly-Scanning Acousto-Optic Tunable Filter for VLSI DRAMs Capacitor Cells
A Precision 60 GHz Open Resonator System for Permittivity and Loss Tangent Measurement of Low Absorbing Materials
abstract: An automated open resonator system is designed and constructed to operate at 60 GHz for loss tangent and permittivity measurement of materials with loss tangent value as low as 10 micro-radians. This is accomplished by the use of a high Q cavity together with a synthesized 60 GHz Gunn oscillator source, a 56 GHz Gunn local oscillator both phase locked to a frequency standard and the heterodyne detection.

articleTitle: Tuning of the Multijunction Thermal Converter for Low Temperature Coefficient of the Output Voltage
Precision Determination of the SI Volt at the PTB
abstract: The measuring system for the determination of the SI volt has been set up and first evaluations of the conversion factor of the volt have been carried out. The voltage balance and all peripheral devices perform as expected, and the applied new measuring method has proved to be suitable. Measuring results with an expected uncertainty of few parts in 10/sup 7/ will be given at the conference.

articleTitle: Direct Measurements of Complex Magnetic Permeability and Complex Dielectric Permittivity of Magnetic Materials
abstract: The dispersive Fourier transform spectroscopy was used with the specimen at the center of a high intensity "Bitter" solenoid magnet to measure the real and imaginary parts of complex magnetic permeability and real and imaginary parts of the complex dielectric permittivity of cubic and hexagonal ferrite materials at millimeter wavelength region.

articleTitle: Calibrator For Alternating Voltage, Current And Power
abstract: A computer-controlled calibrator capable of delivering AC sinusoidal and distorted voltage, current and power, with an accuracy of several parts per milion, is described. A combination of feedback and error-feedforward control strategy, together with the current comparator technique for very accurate ratio measurements, is implemented. The ppm stability of the calibrator permits the use of a multiplexing program for monitoring of several instruments over a long period of time.

articleTitle: High Performance Versatile Semiconductor Laser Diode Doppler Velocimeter
abstract: Described is a new, compact vector-velocimeter setup using a self-mixing type laser diode, which without utilizing frequency-offset devices discriminates direction of target motion with velocity range of 23 mm/s to 3.2 m/s. The range of absolute value velocity measured is 0.2 mm/s to 34 m/s .

articleTitle: The RF Voltage Standard Analysis by Parameter Variation
abstract: The method of the analysis of the thermistor bolometer of the RF voltage standard covering the frequency range up to 1000 MHz is described. The evaluation of the AC/DC difference of the voltage standard is independent of any other RF quantity measurement and serves the accuracy which meets the requirements of the primary standardization.

articleTitle: Accuracy of 30 to 1000 MHz Open Site Acceptance Tests
abstract: In testing EMI radiation measuring sites simplified procedures valid for far field conditions are sometimes used in the inhomogeneous field experienced at short distances from the radiator. Theoretical and experimental errors which may result from such compromises are reviewed and possible ways for their reduction proposed.

articleTitle: An NMR marginal oscillator for measuring magnetic fields below 50 mT
abstract: In order to measure or control magnetic fields in the flux density range from 50 mT down to 1 mT by means of NMR technique, a novel marginal oscillator has been developed. By observing proton resonance in an aqueous CuSO4 solution of about 2 cm3 sample volume, a signal-to-noise ratio of 50 dB has been obtained in a field with a flux density of 15 mT.

articleTitle: Short Baseline Experiments Using the Highly Transportable VLBI Station
abstract: The highly transportable VLBI station is now under development in Radio Research Laboratory. This station consists of a small antenna (diameter:3-m), a compact back-end and a simple frequency standard (crystal oscillator) suitable for a mobile experiment. The preliminary experiments using some parts of the highly transportable VLBI station on short baseline was carried out, and the baseline was determined with almost same precision as an usual VLBI experiment.

articleTitle: Changes in the fundamental constants -- past and future
abstract: The 1986 adjusted values of the fundamental physical constants are assigned significantly improved precision with respect to the uncertainties ascribed to the data in the 1973 adjustment. However, history shows that precision is often not representative of accuracy. This history is reviewed and the reasons for the variations are explored.

articleTitle: Single Optical Pulse Measurement Based on Electro-Optic Sampling
abstract: A single optical pulse measurement has been investigated by an electro-optic sampilng technique. A traveling wave Pockels cell driven by an ultrafast photoconductive switch was employed as a sampler. An optical pulse compression system following a pulsed YAG laser was used as the probe pulse. This technique has a temporal resolution of waveform of the order of 14 ps.

articleTitle: The Baseline Length of Circum-Pacific VLBI Networks and Their Bearing on the Global Tectonics
A Low Field Determination of the Proton Gyromagnetic Ratio in H2O.
Scanning Tunneling Microscopy of the Si-Mosfet Used for Quantized Hall Resistance Measurements
Linear Interpolation of Periodic 633nm in Heterodyne Laser Interferometer for Subnanometer Dimensional Measurement
abstract: The heterodyne laser interferometry is discussed on its accuracy in the subnanometer range for precision dimensional measurement. Simplest optical nonpolarization heterodyne interferometer is tried experimentally in order to eliminate the leakage between reference and measuring optical signal and show that the accuracy around 0.1 nm is achieved.

articleTitle: The Measurement of Optical and Dielectric Properties of Materials
abstract: This paper reviews optical and dielectric measurement techniques developed over approximateiy seventeen years in the frequency range one MHz to 18,000 GHz. It is necessary to employ varieties of measurement techniques to cover this extensive range of frequencies and to cope with material problems such as absorption characterisitics, size, thickness, shape and temperature of specimens.

articleTitle: Optical frequency standards: relations to basic physics and fundamental constants
abstract: The influences of laser spectroscopy and optical frequency standards on basic physics fundamental constants are discussed.

articleTitle: NIM Frequency Stability Measurement System
Supercurrent Graduated in Units of 2ef
abstract: The supercurrent in the V-I characteristics of granular superconducting films is graduated in units of 2ef, in the presence of microwave fields with f = 8-12 GHz, to an accuracy of 200 ppm. This is interpreted in terms of the "Bloch oscillations", which are demonstrated to be dual to the Josephson oscillations.

articleTitle: Measurement of Nanometer Topography by Scanning Tunneling Microscope
abstract: Scanning tunneling microscopes (STM) of two different types were developed for measurement of nanometer order three-dimensional topography. Topographic maps of fine grid patterns on Si substrate fabricated by focused ion-beam lithography, optical grating and a compact disk stamper were obtained with resolution of around 10 nm by using electrochemically formed tips.

articleTitle: FIR Frequency Measurement With A Waveguide-optical Harmonic Mixer
abstract: We report harmonic mixing results of FIR frequencies with a waveguide-optical harmonic mixer using a micrometer-size Schottky-barrier diode which is able to generate high order harmonics at room temperature.

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of Faraday Effect in a Cylindrical Waveguide Containing Ferrite by Spatial Network Method
abstract: Ferrites have been applied to many kind of the nonreciprocal microwave devices. To obtain more exact evaluations of the properties of these devices, it is necessary to be analized on three-dimensional space and time domain. This paper presents the Faraday effect by the spatial network method.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Automated Mrcrowave Permittivity Measurements Using A Six-Port Reflectometer
abstract: A non destructive broad band permittivity measurement method using an automatic six-port reflectometer is presented in this paper. The impedance sensor is an open-ended coaxial line terminated by a semi-infinite medium. This method presents a precision comparable to other methods already in used.

articleTitle: Atomic frequency standards: new trends and progress at nrc
abstract: The paper reviews the state of the art of primary laboratory atomic frequency standards. Emphasis will be put on the new techniques being used in the field such as ion trapping, laser cooling and optical pumping, to implement more accurate primary optical or microwave frequency standards. Progress made at NRC on the subject will be outlined. Finally the central role of time as a base quantity of the international system of units will be discussed.

articleTitle: On The Theories of the Fifth Force
abstract: Theoretical backgrounds behind the experimental searches for a purported intermediate-range force nearly as weak as gravity are reviewed.

articleTitle: Improvements in the Accuracy of a New Coaxial Thermal Noise Standard
Optical Frequency Standards: Present Status And Prospects For The Future
abstract: Progress in the fields of laser frequency stabilization, optical frequency measurements, and high resolution laser spectroscopy opens the possibility to develop optical frequency standards of unpreceded low uncertainty. Basic concepts of such standards are discussed and first experimental results are reviewed. The lowest frequency uncertainties are expected from standards based on slow atomic beams or on stored and cooled ions.

articleTitle: A Series of Program for Measuring the Correction to the Calculated Field Due to Iron in the Earth
Phase-shift in the ramsey-type cavity of the Kg standard
abstract: The cavity phase-shift is, at the moment, the most important error source in the Mg beam frequency standard. An evaluation of this effect is given for the present experimental set-up and possible improvements are discussed in order to reduce its contribution to the 10/sup -13/ level.

articleTitle: Uncertainty in a Calibration of a Photodiode Type Power Meter Due to Spectral Width of a Light Source
abstract: An error due to a spectral width of a light source in a calibration of a photodiode type power meter has been studied. Three types of Si, Ge and InGaAs photodiode have been examined in the wavelength of 750~1700nm. A theoretical calculation has shown that more than 5% error arises on a Si or a Ge photodiode in a specific wavelength region. A measured difference between two photodiode type power meter agreed the theoretically estimated difference within 0.5%.

articleTitle: Extremely Low Frequency Noise in Oscillators
abstract: In the present contribution we have shown the 1/f/sup 2/ noise in oscillators need not be neceesarily generated by environmental temperature fluctuations. As a consequence we investigate a possible theoretical evidence for the relationship between 1/f and l/f/sup 2/ noises.

articleTitle: Development Of A Noise Calibraition System At NRC
A New Isothermal Multijunction Differential Thermal Element Provides Fast Settling AC to DC Converters
abstract: A new isothermal AC-DC transfer element has been reduced to practice. Constructed as a dual heater hot wire device it maintains high precision, with usable frequency capability beyond 100 MHz while settling to final value in several hundred milliseconds. The fast response substantially speeds operation of automated ac-dc transfer standards and precison ac digital voltmeters.

articleTitle: A stabilized optical source with laser diode for distance measurement
Development of Coordinate Measuring Equipment Using Electromagnetic Give and Receive Action Method
abstract: We designed a new coordinate measuring equipment that uses the LC resonant circuit. The pointing devices of this equipment have no cords and no batteries and dose not directly contact the sensor board. It can measure coordinates at an accuracy of up to 0.1mm and also detect the state of the switch.

articleTitle: Optimum Dimention of Mount for Measurement of Permittivity
abstract: The experimental results on the effect of the geometry of mount on permittivity of dielectric materials are described.The condition, ka=0, make the field distribution in the mount uniform. In case of ka>0.5, the mount has not uniform field and the experimental results lead to noticeable error.

articleTitle: Wide-Range Automated System for Measuring Standard Resistors
A 10 kW Class Calorimeter for CW-CO/sub 2/ Laser Power Measurements
Modeling of Multilayer Thick Film Components Using Time Domain Techniques
abstract: A technique for modeling multilayer thick film components using time domain measurements is presented. A multilayer inductor, formed by stacking spiral coils vertically with intervening dielectric layer, is used to demonstrate the technique. The component under test is placed at the end of a reference line, and a TDR waveform is acquired. A physically based model is developed to fit the TDR information.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electric Field for Measurement While Drilling Using Combined FEM with BEM
abstract: To establish EM-MWD (Electromagnetic Measurement While Drilling) technology, we analyze the electric field around a drillstring, using a computer simulation based on combined FEM (Finite Element Method) with BEM (Boundary Element Method) developed by us. The verification of this simulation method is shown by an experimental system using a water tank.

articleTitle: Convenient Error Estimating Method for Current Transformer Test System Using Current Comparator
An electromagnetic field distortion measurement system
abstract: A quaternion process on EM field data provide a precise six degree-of-freedom measure of position/field distortion between two low frequency variously polarized probes. The technique suggests other fundamental EM field measurement applications which relate to certain types of scattering and field distorting environments.

articleTitle: Time-Division Multiplication in Wideband Application
abstract: A solution for high accuracy electric power measurements for distorted input signals on industrial frequencies (50, 60 Hz) is presented. An improvement in the method of time-division technics is introduced and it refutes the oppinions that time-division technics is not convenient for wideband applications. The accuracy of the realised model is on the 100 ppm level for industrial frequency signals measurements with 100% harmonic distorsion up to 1 kHz.

articleTitle: An Accurate Automated 10-Volt Measuring System
abstract: An automated system to measure dc voltages to 10 V is described. It consists of an accurate, self checking resistive voltage divider, a scanner and a reference voltage source. Under the programmed control of a microcomputer, it has proven to be particularly useful in the calibration of groups of solid-state voltage standards.

articleTitle: Remote Refractive Indices Difference Meter for Salinity Sensor
abstract: Remote refractive indices difference meter was designed and tested for use of salinity sensor. The principle is to measure the difference between the real sea water's indices and the standard water's. It is composed of a semiconductor laser, a partitioned water cell and a solid position detector. The performance of the sensor is also described.

articleTitle: Automatic Time Domain Measurement System
abstract: This paper describes an Automatic Time - Domain Measurement System ( ATDMS ) developed by NIM . This system has the feature of good accurcy, multifunction, fast speed and high performance / price ratio. The basic function and error analysis are given.

articleTitle: Improvements in the Absolute Determination of the Farad and the OHM at LCIE
abstract: Following the 1986 experiments performed at LCIE concerning the absolute determination of the Farad and the Ohm, some improvements were made on the main parts, the calculable cylindrical capacitor, the capacitance bridges and the quadrature bridge.

articleTitle: Velocity Selecting Ramsey Fringe Spectroscopy of Calcium Intercombination Transition Utilizing Further Longitudinal Excitation
abstract: A Scheme of the velocity selecting Ramsey fringe spectroscopy utilizing a further longitudinal excitation to a higher lying shortlived state is presented and examined for the realization of a new wavelength/ frequency standard based on the Ca intercombination transition.

articleTitle: Real Time Measurement of Methane Concentration in the Atmosphere
abstract: A system has been developed which is capable of measuring methane concentration over a wide area using a 3.39-um He-Ne laser. The laser is of a type commercially available, and the system is a fixed one. Detection of about 100 ppm.m concentration is presently possible.

articleTitle: Precision AC Measurement of Temperature Below 90K
abstract: This paper illustrates the level of precision and accuracy attainable using AC techniques for intercomparing intrinsic temperature standards between 10K and 90K.

articleTitle: SI Value of Qunatized Hall Resistance Based on ETL's Calculable Capacitor
abstract: SI value of quantized Hall resistanee based on ETL's calculable capacitor is presented. Some improvements of previous measurement systems were prooeeded and some parts of the measurement techniques were changed. The measurements are now in progress. We will present more reliable results than the previous one in CPEM'88.

articleTitle: The 1987 International Comparison of One-OHM Resistance Standards at the BIPM and the Resulting Agreement Among Determination of RH
abstract: To evaluate the agreement among determinations of the quantized Hall resistance, RH, in terms of national representations of the ohm, the BIPM organized and conducted an international comparison of one-ohm resistance standards among twelve laboratories. A relative uncertainty of about 2 x 10-8 is expected for some of the resistance comparisons. Resulting values of RH will be presented.

articleTitle: Step Attenuator for Multimode Fiber Optics and its Calibration
abstract: The structure and charactristics of a fiber optic step attenuator which is improved on the spectral dependency are described. The calibration system is also introduced.

articleTitle: Recharacterization of thermal voltage converters after thermoelement replacement
abstract: This paper describes the relationship between the characteristics of various thermoelements (TE's) as voltage or ourrent converters and the overall ac-dc differences of a voltage range. An algorithm is presented to predict the ac-dc differences of series resistors with different TE's, and a method for recharacterizing a thermal voltage converter containing a replacement TE is given. The measured results show that for most applications, a complete recharacterization of the TVC set is unnecessary.

articleTitle: Quasi-Optically Coupled Harmonic Mixer in the Submillimeter Wave Region
A Method for Simultaneously Measuring Resistivity and the Meissner Effect of a Superconductor Used with a Solenoid Coil
abstract: From the differences in reactance and resistance between a circular solenoid coil surrounding and coaxial with a cylindrical conductor and a similar coil without the conductor, a method for measuring resistivity and permeability of the conductor is proposed. The resistivity of copper measured by this method has correlated well with the values measured by the DC four-probe method. Furthermore, the experiment with a high Tc superconductor indicates that the resistivity and permeability of the conductor can be measured with remarkable accuracy.

articleTitle: Optical Fiber Feedback Squid Magnetometer
Intercomparison of RF and Microwave Standards
abstract: In order to harmonize RF and microwave standards, intercomparisons have been organized by several organisms. They are reviewed in terms of participants, frequency spectrum covered, quantities and achieved results. Finally the need of new intercomparisons to organize is showed.

articleTitle: Precision Measurement of Quantized Hall Resistance and Determination of the Fine-Structure Constant
abstract: This paper describes the methods used at the PTB to determine the fine-structure constant by precision measurements of quantized Hall resistances in combination with determination of the SI ohm. Numerical results together with a detailed uncertainty budget will be given at the conference.

articleTitle: Electrical Measurement System in the Federal Republic of Germany
abstract: Before 1900 the Electrical Measurement System in Germany was founded based on the "Law on electrical Units" from 1898. This paper describes the present status of the tasks and organization of the legal and the industrial metrology in the area of electricity in the Federal Republic of Germany and West Berlin. The "Deutscher Kalibrierdienst" DKD, which was founded 1977, assures traceability to national standards of measurements done in industry for quality control. The links of the German Electrical Measurement System to international organizations and institutions are given.

articleTitle: Time Comparisons Between KSRI and RRL via the Geostationary Meteorological Satellite of Japan
abstract: A time comparison system using the ranging signal of the Geostationary Meteorological Satellite of Japan (GMS) has been developed, and the GMS measurements have been carried out between KSRI and RRL.

articleTitle: The Effects Of Acoustic Gravity Wave In Atmosphere On The Precision Time Transmission And Positioning System
abstract: In this paper we discuss the variation of the atmospheric index of refraction caused by acoustic gravity wave (AGW) of artifitial and natural source and its (AGW's) effects on the wave propogation in microwave frequency band between ground and space and in low frequency.

articleTitle: New Reflection Coefficient Formula With Higher Precision in Six-Port
abstract: In this paper, a new formula to calculate load reflection coefficient is derived using absolute power theory of six-port measurement system. The computer simulation and experiment all show that in the presence of noise this formula is more precise than the one we used generally.

articleTitle: 30MHz Attenuation Standard Using Binary Phase Modulation Method
abstract: 30MHz attenuation measurement system which uses a ratio transformer as the standard attenuator instead of a piston attenuator is designed and examined. Higher accuracy at low attenuations and easier maintenance are expected in the system than in the conventional one. Homodyne detection for the binary phase modulation method and heterodyne detection for the intermediate frequency substitution method are examined for 30MHz-1KHz attenuation conversion.

articleTitle: Linearity of quantized voltages generated by a josephson junction array
abstract: Linearity of quantized voltages generated by a Josephson junction array is experimentally tested at every 100mV in a voltage range of 100mV to 1 volt. The priciple is to measure the resistance ratios of resistors connected in series and examining the consistency among the resistance ratios. The accuracy of measurement is expected to be few parts in 10/sup 8/.

articleTitle: National Measurement System in India
abstract: In Indla, about 130 calibration laboratories and 300 testing laboratories are functioning. These laboratories are now to be given formal accreditation under the National Coordination of Testing and Calibration Facilities (NCTCF) Programme of the Govt. of Indla. NCTCF has two components (a) Calibration Service Programme and (b) Accreditatlon Programme for Testing Laboratories. This paper outlines the organization of NCTCF and describes the salient features of the Calibration Service Programme.

articleTitle: Calibration of the Delay Time in the GPS and GMS Time Comparison Receivers of Japan and Australia Using Portable Reference Receivers
abstract: In November and December 1987, the portable receiver experiment was performed betwene Japan and Australia to calibrate the delay time in GPS and GMS time comparison receivers. By the calibration the accuracy of GPS and GMS time comparison was improved to be 70ns.

articleTitle: Optical Ftber Length Measurement By External Phase Modulatton Type Optical Heterodyne Reflectometry
abstract: An optical fiber length measuring method using an external phase modulation type reflectometry is proposed and experimentally-demonstrated. Use of a gas laser light source and external fiber phase modulator exclude destabilizing effect of direct modulation scheme. Typical experimental results of fiber length measurements by changing its length stepwise indicate high agreement with real length.

articleTitle: The new concept of three-terminal admittance bridge with selfcalibration ability
abstract: The theory and the example of the concrete configuration of the bridge for three-terminal admittance measurement with selfcalibration ability is described. The new approach enabled to realize a simple bridge circuit with non-iterative calibration procedure which allows to meet the highest metrological requirements.

articleTitle: Experimental confirmation of the aharonov-bohm effect
abstract: Experimental evidence was obtained for the existence of the AB effect. This effect has been a subject of long controversy regarding the physical significance of gauge fields, -- in the present case, the vector potentials.

articleTitle: Earth Rotation Parameters Determined By VLBI
abstract: Analyses of the UTI- and pole series (splitted up into alongtrack components and crosstrack components) of the IRIS and other VLBI Earth rotation programs involving the Wettzell radio telescope are presented, which reveal several short period oscillations. These can be related either to atmospheric or to tidal excitation.

articleTitle: Progress in VLBI at Shanghai Observatory
abstract: This report presents an overview of recent developments on VLBI in Shanghai Observatory. The Shanghai Radio Station equipped with 25 meter antenna and other facilities was operational last year. The VLBI data processing system has been set up recently. It includes the S-2 VLBI data processor and a series of post correlation processing programs for astronomy as well as geodesy.

articleTitle: Measurement of h/e/sup 2/ at IMS & IMM
Evaluation and utilization of the Josephson array
abstract: A system using a Josephson series array capable of developing voltages of up to 1.3 volts is described. The array system has been compared to Volt NRC with good agreement. The applications and implications of the array system are examined.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Contact-Free Detection of Current Noise
abstract: A configuration for the detection of current noise is proposed, in which no electrical contacts to the sample under measurement are necessary. The threshold sensitivity of the detection of the current fluctuation can be considerabily improved by producing a cross spectrum between the sideband fluctuations of the two carriers.

articleTitle: Measurement System in Thailand
abstract: As the industrial science and technology became wider in range and higher in technical requirements, the need for measuring techniques and standards has expanded, generally seeking for a higher accuracy. The measurement system in Thailand should be developed in the national calibration centre, along with active research and development activities in many fields. These activities are necessary to guarantee the quality of the Thai Industrial products.

articleTitle: Pulse Spreading Due to Polarization Dispersion in Single-Mode Fibers
Author index
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: 1988 Conference On Precision Electromagnetic Measurements [front matter]
abstract: Conference proceedings front matter may contain various advertisements, welcome messages, committee or program information, and other miscellaneous conference information. This may in some cases also include the cover art, table of contents, copyright statements, title-page or half title-pages, blank pages, venue maps or other general information relating to the conference that was part of the original conference proceedings.

articleTitle: A New Power Standard of Audio Frequency
abstract: A new thermal power comparator of audio frequency has been developed, which is essentially a double bridge-type multipliers comprlsed of two multijunction thermal converters, containing two heaters. Together with a precision inductive voltage divider and current transformer for extending voltage and current range, the comparator enables establish a high precision power standard with ac-dc transfer error less than 15 ppm in audio frequency range.

articleTitle: Measurement of high-frequency current distribution on a planar conductor
abstract: In the measurement of current distribution on a planar conductor or antenna with a small shielded loop, the electromotive force induced on the loop is theoretically formulated and the relation between current distribution and measured values is investigated. As an experimental example a square patch microstrip antenna is given.

articleTitle: The Prediction of the E.M.F. Stability of the High Precision Saturated Cadmium Sulfate Standard Cells
abstract: This paper briefly analyses the various factors which may cause the cell's emf increasing or decreasing. The different method to predict the emf stability of 1-2 ppm high precision standard cells has been described here. Experimental results have shown that among these methods the emf hysteresis effect test method recommended in GB3929-83 is most valuable.

articleTitle: Performance of the Quantum Hall Effect Resistance Standard at IMS
Toward the Avogadro Constant - Preliminary Results on the Molar Volume of Silicon
abstract: The silicon molar volume has been measured through Atomic Weight and density measurements. Mass spectrometric determination of the isotopic composition was performed on two differently grown samples. Density of specimens from the same crystals was obtained through mass and direct dimension measurements on single crystal spheres.

articleTitle: Quantized Hall Resistance Measurements
Optical Time-Domain Calibration Device
abstract: Optical time-domain reflectomers fond many applications including the installation, commissioning and maintenance for optical fiber videocommunication systems measurements. In order to test and calibrate them a new type of test device is proposed. The described passive device is compact and easy to operate making it ideal for field use.

articleTitle: Development of GPS Positioning System "PRESTAR"
abstract: The relative positioning system using GPS, called "PRESTAR", has been developing by the Radio Research Laboratory, Japan. It is designed to obtain high accurate relative position and precise orbit. The short baseline test was successfully conducted. The long baseline positioning experiments and orbit determination experiments are planned this year.

articleTitle: Audio-frequency current-comparator power bridge
abstract: A system for performing active and reactive power measurements from 50 Hz to 20 kHz is described. The technique is an extension of a power bridge based on a current comparator capacitance bridge that was originally restricted to power frequencies. A digitally-synthesized dual-channel signal source provides the required voltage and current signals.

articleTitle: Preliminary Results at I.M.G.C. in the Absolute Determination of the Silicon d
abstract: This papev summarizes the wovk at I.M.G.C. on the combined x-ray and optical interferometers at present in use to measure the

articleTitle: EM Measurements of the Velocity of Light
The System for Measurement of Birefringence by the Use of Photo Elastic Modulator and its Applications
abstract: The system to measure very small optical birefringence such as for an opticaI data storage disk and thin films is described. As the optical system utilizes a photo elastic modulator, measured data includes not only the accurate value of retardation but also a direction of fast axis of retardation. Some of its applications are discussed.

articleTitle: Precise Satellite Orbit Determination And Gravity Recovery With The Global Positioning Systek
abstract: The Global Positioning System will be used for differential positioning of low earth orbiting satellites with unprecedented accuracies. This in turn will lead to major improvements in ocean circulation information obtained from altimetric missions and in the geopotential model obtained from gravity missions.

articleTitle: Stable gas-dielectric capacitors of 5pF and 10pF
abstract: Gas-dielectric capacitors of 5pF and 10pF have been developed for use as standards in NML and KSRI. They are stable with time, have small temperature and voltage coefficients, and have been used successfully as travelling standards.

articleTitle: A Criterion to Identify the Ambiguity in Relative Power Five-Port Theory
abstract: A formula to calculate reflection coefficient in an arbitary five-port is derived in this paper according to absolute power theory. Although the precision of this formula is a little lower than that of relative power five-port theory in most case, it can he used as a criterion to identify the ambiguity in relative power five-port theory.

articleTitle: An Improved Cryogenic Current Compartor
Determination of the Time-Dependence of the NBS OHM Using the Quantized Hall Resistance
abstract: The quantum Hall effect is being used to monitor the U.S. legal unit of resistance NBS. Measurements have been made on a regular basis since August 1983. This paper will discuss the history, the improvement, and the results of these measurements.

articleTitle: Experimental Results on Gas-Lens Effects in (He-Ne)/CH/sub 4/ Lasers (/spl lambda/= 3.39 /spl mu/m)
abstract: Design criteria have been established allowing the cancellation of spurious frequency offsets induced by gas-lens effects in He-Ne lasers stabilized by saturated absorption in an intra-cavity absorber cell. They have been checked experimentally using a specially designed laser. Good agreement is generally found between theory and experiment in spite of unexplained effects at low modulation amplitudes. Also observed in this special laser is the output effect, i.e. the frequency change which occurs when the photodetector used for servo-control is at one end or the other end of the resonator.

articleTitle: A proposal on a multijunction thermal converter
abstract: The authers propose a kind of multijunction thermal converter (MJTC) as ac-dc transfer standsrds. The MJTC consists of 44 pairs of thermocouples composed of bismuth aad antimony on a mica substrate. Each junctin of thermocouples is serially connected and alined alternatively on two strigth lines. A heater made of a high resistive fine wire is adhered on a line of the junctions to make hot junctions of the thermocouples. A thick copper plate covered with a vinyl sheet is fixed on other line of the junctions to make cold junctions. Ac-dc transfer differences of the thin film MJTCs are compared with that of singl junction thermal converters(SJTC). The measured data show that ac-dc transfer difference of MJTCs is greater than that of SJTCs ky about a few ppm.

articleTitle: Improving Precision of System Constants in Six-Port by Means of Lagrange's Multipliers Method
abstract: A method is described in this paper which can further correct the error in system constants calibrated and improve its precision. This method use only nine unknown load and no standard. It is proved in computer simulation.

articleTitle: Measurement of electrode surface effects on air capacitors using precise coulombmeter
abstract: A method by which the alr capacitor electrodes are charged wlth the DC voltage and then quickly discharged is described. Immediately afterwards, a very sensitlve coulombmeter ls switched on to measure the additlonal discharging in the thin dielectric fllm. The method enables the measurement of effects with a time constant of several milliseconds to several thousand seconds.

articleTitle: Permittivity Measurements of Macroscopic Particles
abstract: Non-uniform electric fields are used to determine the dielectric properties of macroscopic particles (um). Experimental work on permittivity measurements of microfossils have led to new applications in paleontology.

articleTitle: Precision Coaxial and Waveguide Microcalorimeters for RF and Microwave Power Standards
abstract: Four sets of coaxial and waveguide microcalorimeters for measuring the effective efficiencies of thermistor mounts are described. The results of effective efficiency measurements are reported and the uncertainty analysis of the system is briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Recent Determinations of RH in Terms of /spl Omega/60-BI
Australia's National Measurement System
abstract: Australia has a well-established, decentralised National Measurement system. CSIRO's National Measurement Laboratory maintains the national standards of measurement, the National Association of Testing Authorities accredits calibration and testing laboratories, and the National Standards Commission is responsible for legal metrology and trade measurement.

articleTitle: Organization of Metrology and Calibration Services in France
abstract: This paper describes the organization of the metrology in France, the different laboratories in which are defined and maintained national standards and the accreditation system which insure the traceability of the industry to those standards.

articleTitle: Measurement Standards For Single-Mode Fibers
abstract: Standard measurement procedures for single-mode fibers are reviewed. Various methods are evaluated and agreement accuracy discussed.

articleTitle: 1/f noise in electrical components caused by the positive thermal feedback in self-generating syste
abstract: The positive thermal feedback in a self-generating system is shown to convert thermally induced white noise into 1/f noise. According to this model the slope of the low frequency noise spectrum is very close to unity since the real component evacuates its heat into the three-dimensional space. The theory predicts that the 1/f noise exceeds white noise below the frequency characterizing both the geometric structure of the component and the thermal properties of the surroundings. Consequently, the uncertainty of the measurement is inversely proportional to the physical size of the component or the standard.

articleTitle: Present International Status of Microwave Power Standards
abstract: This paper presents an upto date informatlon on various techniques being used for the precise measurement of microwave power in National Standards Laboratories of various countries includinq the capabilities attained by NPL, India in this field. Various aspects, such as design and fabrication, operational simplicity, limitations, etc., of the techniques have been discussed. The uncertainty achieved in the determination of effective efficiency of the mounts by different techniques has also been given.

articleTitle: Japan-US Time Comparison Experiment Better than 1 Nano-Second Accuracy by Using a Radio Interferometric Technique
abstract: Zero Baseline Interferometry (ZBI) experiment was conducted to determine the differential instrumental delay between Japan and USA. It enables us an absolute time comparison of the accuracy better than 1.0ns.

articleTitle: Realization of the S.I. Ampere by an Integration Method
abstract: A study of realization of the S.I. ampere by an integration method is in progress to contribute for redetermination of the S.I. ampere at ETL. Preparation of a measuring apparatus based on the method has been almost completed, and preliminalry experiment will soon be began.

articleTitle: Current measurement systems by utilizing cryogenic techniques for the absolute magnetic flux quantum measurement
Traceability System of Electrical Standards in Japan
abstract: This paper describes the traceability system of electrical standards in Japan. National standards are established and maintained by ETL. The dissemination of electrical standards has been carried out by the intermediate transfer agencies, JEMIC and JMI, since 1965.

articleTitle: Research Activities on Standard Time and Frequency Signal Dissemination Using Communication Satellite Links
Measurement Of The Optical Power Generated Through Four-Wave Mixing Process In A Dispersion-Shifted Single-Mode Optical Fiber
abstract: Optical powers generated through four-wave mixing process in single-mode transmission lines are measured by the teehnique utilizing a heterodyne receiver and a lock-in detector. The generated powers of approximately 0.2 nW are measured suceessfully for input powers below 1 mW at the wavelengths of 1286 nm and 155O nm.

articleTitle: The Millimeter Accuracy of the Geodetic VLBI Measurements Achieved on a 54-KM Base Line
abstract: The millimeter accuracy of the geodetic VLBI measurements was demonstrated in the experiments repeated 4 times on a 54-km baseline between a 5-m transportable antenna at Tsukuba and a 26-m antenna at Kashima. The error analysis shows that the thermal reeeiver noise is a main cause of the delay observation error and the atmospheric fluctuations mainly affect on the delay rate observations.

articleTitle: A 10-V Josephson voltage standard
abstract: This paper describes the design and operation of an 18 992 Josephson junction array which can generate reference voltages up to 10 V.

articleTitle: The Generation of Laser Difference Frequencies Using the Scanning Tunneling Microscope
abstract: Infrared laser radiation and radio-frequency signals were coupled into the tunneling junction of a scanning tunneling microscope and the difference frequencies and their harmonics generated in the nonlinear junction were studied as a function of the tunneling parameters. The importance of the results for the difference-frequency mixing in metal-insulator-metal diodes and for the scanning tunneling microscope is discussed.

articleTitle: Determination of Scattering Parameters from Precision Coaxial Air-Line Standards
abstract: Scattering parameter expressions are developed for the principal mode of a coaxial air line. Dimensional variations in the inner and outer conductors and skin effect are included in the model. An error analysis reveals accuracy of the scattering parameters is primarily dependent on the conductor radii measurements precision.

articleTitle: A new method of improving the accuracy for calibrating micropotentiometer
A Method of Evaluating the Noise Temperature of Microwave Thermal Noise Sources by Using Three Transmission Lines
abstract: A new method is proposed to evaluate the noise temperature of a microwave thermal noise source composed of a termination and a transmission line. The noise temperature correction of its transmission line can be easily determined by employing three transmission lines to which its termination should be connected in order.

articleTitle: Towards the realisation of an atomic standard of mass
abstract: Summary form only given. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings. The kilogram is a base SI unit, and is defined as the 'mass of the international prototype of the kilogram'. It thereby survives as the last of the artefact standards and it is natural to enquire how long it will continue to do so. The last two decades have shown an increasing use of quantum phenomenae in metrology at the very highest accuracy. The history of metrology shows that the practical realisation of a concept can take many years to bring to a viable working reality. The development of a natural atomic mass standard is just one more example of this. The paper will discuss the evolution of an atomic mass standard in terms of the above and it will review the current state of the art of mass measurement and future prospects.

articleTitle: New Improvement on Nim's Cesium Beam Primary Frequency Standard CS III
Improvement of the Superconducting Magnetic Levitation System for the Determination of the Magnetic Flux Quantum
abstract: An improvement of the preliminary superconducting magnetic levitation system, including an introduction of the Josephson electronic devices, is in progress for the absolute determination of the magnetic flux quantum.

articleTitle: An improved transportable dc voltage standard
abstract: Commercially-available dc voltage references have been found to be less than optimum for transferring a unit of voltage. The design and construction of an improved transport standard producing 10 V and 1.018 V is discussed.

articleTitle: Development of a Scanning Tunneling Microscope for Operation in Air
abstract: We have constructed an scanning tunneling microscope (STM) appropriate for application in air. Observation is possible in wide range from subnanometer order to micrometer order. Reliable and convenient operation is performed by rigid and symmetric mechanical structure of the STM unit with vibration isolate system.

articleTitle: A Calcium Frequency Standard: Frequency Stabilization By Means Of Nonlinear Ramsey Resonances
Precise Measurements of Dissipation Factor in Microwave Printed Boards
abstract: A precise method for separating the dissipation factor associated with both dielectric losses and conductor losses of printed circuit boards through wide range of microwave frequencies is presented. This method accomplishes the separation by utilizing the difference in dependence of the two losses on the dimensions in triplate-line resonators composed of printed circuit boards.

articleTitle: Measurement Of The Complex Permittivity Of Microwave Materials With A Submillimeter Waveguide Four-Port Reflectometer
abstract: A new four-port reflectometer for the determination of the complex relative permittivity of microwave materials at submillimeter wavelengths is described. Measurement results obtained with various low-loss solids at frequencies of about 380 GHz agree well with data taken from the literature or obtained as results of an international comparison measurement exercise.

articleTitle: Accuracy of the ftne structure constant
abstract: At present the fine structure constant /spl alpha/ can be determined with a precision of better than few parts in 10/sup 7/ in four independent ways. They are based on the ac Josephson effect, the quantized Hall effect, the muonium hfs, and the anomalous magnetic.moment of the electron. Further improvements of these results and their implications to physics and metrology will be discussed.

articleTitle: Microwave Radiometer Calibration and its Error Analysis
abstract: This paper describes the meaning of radiometer calibration, the calibration methods, classification, and the comparison of the methods, classification, and the comparison of the methods, especially discusses the two-point itemized calibration equation and its error sources. It also analyses the calibration error caused by system mismatch in detail and quantitively estimates its error value. We've used above method to calibrate K and K a band radiometers.

articleTitle: An Algorithm for the Least-Squares Adjustment Based on Classification and Generalization
abstract: An objective algorithm for the least-squares adjustment is proposed. Modification is applied to a limited number of given items in a generalized way. Exclusion is applied successively to a single item when the result of modificatioin is anomalous. Final result is a median value of modification.

articleTitle: Low Phase Noise YTO Synthesizer
abstract: We have developed the synthesizer, YIG Tuned Oscillator (YTO), capable of setting the frequency of the microwave bands from 100 KHz to 4.5 GHz accurately using 0.1 Hz resolution and having superior spectrum purity where the SSB phase noise in 4 GHz output frequency is -129 [dBc/Hz] (10 KHz from the carrier).

articleTitle: Progress in Optigal Frequengy Measurement At NRLM
Development of 10 Meter Laser Interferometer Gravitational Wave Antenna
abstract: A delay-line type of a laser interferometer with an arm length of 10 meter for detecting gravitational wave is under construction, a large antenna in space being as a future target. 4 bounce operation has been completed and the final goal is about 100 bounce operation ( an effective arm length of 1 km ) with a sensitivity determined by the shot noise.

articleTitle: Optical Power Meter Calibration Based on Stabilized Green He-Ne Laser and Cryogenic Absolute Radiometer
Characteristics Of The Optically Pumped CS Frequency Standard At The NRLM
abstract: At the National Research Laboratory of Metrology [NRLM], we are developing an optically pumped Cs frequency standard, its design and present performance are reported here.

articleTitle: Reference Pulse Generators: Theory Application and Status of Development
abstract: The reference pulse generator (RPG) is a transfer standard, i.e., a generator of known pulse shape, amplitude, and source impedance, useful for evaluating the measurement capabilities of waveform measurement systems. The discussion includes (1) principles, (2) application methodology, and (3) a review of the RPG evolution to present ongoing development.

articleTitle: Intercomparison Of NBS Noise Calibration Services
abstract: New, less restrictive thermal noise calibration services recently established in the frequency range of 2 - 12.4 GHz overlap prior NBS services and provide an opportunity for intercomparison. The agreement between old and new calibration systems is better than 0.4%

articleTitle: Compact frequency stabilized laser using AiGaAs laser
A New Multifunctional Digital Instrumentation
abstract: A new multifunctional digital instrumentation is presented in this paper, which consists of multiplex, analog-to-digital converter (CAD), frequency-to-digital converter (FDC), single-chip-microcomputer, keyboard, digital display and printer. It can measure seven analog signals and two frequency signals. The analog signals are the output signals of analog transducers. The frequency signals may be the output signals of the transducers with frequency output. Besides, some main special functions of this digital instrument are: automatic compensation of temperature and source voltage fluctuation.

articleTitle: Time Domain Dielectric Spectroscopy Using a Wideband Dielectric Filled Cavity
abstract: This paper presents a new sample holder to be used for the characterization of dielectric materials over a wide band of frequencies. The dielectric fills a cylindrical cavity which is adapted to 50 ohm precision air line(s). The scattering parameters, measured in the time domain, are used to determine the complex dielectric constant of the material.

articleTitle: Improvement of frequency accuracy in a zemicondoctor laser pumped /sup 87/Rb atomic clock
abstract: Light shift of rubidium atomic clock was accurately measured. By controlling the laser frequency detuning based on the results of the measurements, the microwave frequeney inaccuracy of a rubidium atomic clock was reduced to t3.2x10/sup -11/.

articleTitle: Precise Measurement of Photo-Diodes' Spectral Responses Using Calorimetric Method
Effect of Buffer Gas on the Total Number and the Storage Time of BA Ions Trapped in an RF Ion Trap
abstract: The total number and the storage time of Ba ions trapped in an rf ion trap were determined under various pressures of buffer gas. It was found that addition of any kind of buffer gas in the ion trap enlarged the total number but that of light gas was effective in lengthening the storage time of Ba ions.

articleTitle: Waveform Monitoring of Single-Shot Laser Pulse with an Optical Circuit
abstract: Real-time waveform monitoring of single-shot subnanosecond laser-pulse is made possible using an optical fiber circuit. This method is based on convolution between delayed signals and a single step function, implemented by multiple optical fibers and a bulk-type LiTaO3 Pockel's cell as a gate driven by Auston switch. Architecture of the system and experimental results showing a temporal resolution of 0.5ns are reported, along with advances in integration of the gate on a planar LiTa03 substrate for higher temporal resolution.

articleTitle: A Controlling And Data Acquisition System For The Reference Diffuse Reflectance Spectrophotometer Based On The IBM-PC/XT Computer
abstract: A System has been designed for controlling, acquiring and storing the photoelectric signals for the reference reflectance spectrophotometer in the division of radiometric physics at the NBS. Based on the IBM-PC/XT computer system, the GPIB interface is chosen to connect with various instruments (such as, current amplifier, lock-in amplifier, digital voltmeter and programmable high voltage power supply etc.) The control and analysis program is written in the TBASIC programming language. This system can also be used to control several stepping motors, as well as to control the opening and closing of the shutters. This computer program can be used for both the visible spectrum region from 200 to 750 NM and the near infrared region from 750 to 2500 NM. In this paper, the reference reflectance spectrophotometer, the computer program, and the resutts of the performance test are described.

articleTitle: Analysis For Vacuo-Thermojunction Characteristics Using Microcomputer
abstract: Fourier analysis technique is adopted to evaluate the dc and ac component in a thermo-electromotive force (TEMF) from a vacuo-thermojunction(VTJ) at ultra-low frequency. In experiments, a digital wavememory(DM) and a microcomputer(MC) are used to minimize a noise by repeating the analysis and averaging each results. A number of repetition required to sufficiently suppress the influence of the noise is given.

articleTitle: Theory and measurements of unintentional radiators
abstract: By characterizing an unknown emitter with equivalent vector electric- and magnetic - dipole moments, we formulate a theoretical basis to express the radiation properties of such an emitter in terms of these unknown dipole moments. Power and relative phase measurements from appropriate ports of a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell when the emitter is placed at the cell's center are proven to be sufficient to determine quantitatively the unknowns and therefore, the radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: An International Comparison of Power Meter Calibrations Conducted in 1987
abstract: The results of an intercomparison of power meter calibrations conducted during 1987 between the National Research Council, Ottawa, the National Bureau of Standards, Gaithersburg, and the Physikalisch Technische Bundesanstalt, Braunschweig, using a time-division multipiler watt-converter developed at the Institut Mihailo Pupin, Belgrade, are described. The measurements were made at 120 volts, 5 amperes, 50 and 60 hertz, at power factors of 1.0, 0.5 lead and lag, and 0.0 lead and lag. An agreement between the laboratories of better than 20 parts in a million is indicated.

articleTitle: Accurate gain measurement of horn antennas in the shortened far field
12 Bit/25.6M sps Subranging A/D Converter
A Current-Dividing-Type High Stable DC Current Transformer Using a Magnetic Modulator
abstract: A high stable(lppm) large dc current transformer is described. It is constructed using a current dividing network by shunt resistors and two magnetic-modulator-type ampere-turn comparators. The transform ratio of the transformer is independent of the current ratio in the shunt resistors.

articleTitle: On-Fiber Sensor and Modulator
abstract: The developed on-fiber technique, that makes part of an optical fiber into an electromagnetic field sensor and modulator, is presented. The principle of this technique is to replace the passive cladding material surrounding a short section of the fiber core with an active material, which is sensitive to electromagnetic fields.

articleTitle: Data Reconstruction by Interleaved Sampling
abstract: According to the Sarnpling Theorem, a given signal must be bandlimited to fo / 2 (fo is the sampling frequency) to be recoverable from its sampling data. In this paper, however, it is shown that by using several trains of interleaved sampling data, this limit can be expanded.

articleTitle: Industrial Experience with an Intelligent AC/DC Standard
abstract: AC-DC voltage standards based entirely on solid state references, used as secondary, working or transfer standards, are widely used although metrological performance is typically defined only via comparison with a higher level standard.
